title: Strong bounded-error randomized recognition
statement: A language $L$ of Boolean strings has strong randomized polynomial-time recognition with parameter $d$ if there are a Boolean-valued verifier $M$, natural numbers $a,k$, and an efficient verifier induced by $M$, such that for every input $x$, if $x\in L$, then with a polynomially bounded number of fair random bits the probability that $M$ accepts is at least $1-(1/2)^{(|x|+1)^d+1}$; if $x\notin L$, the probability that it rejects is at least the same bound.
hypotheses_covered: There exists a verifier on pairs of Boolean strings
There exist natural numbers a and k
The verifier induced by M is efficient
For every input string x, acceptance probability has the stated lower bound when x belongs to L
For every input string x, rejection probability has the stated lower bound when x does not belong to L
caveat: The supplied snippet does not define the efficiency predicate, polyLen, or randProb, so their precise meanings cannot be made self-contained from this payload.
